Format on save, a setting, formats code with its language server or formatter before it is written
Auto save after a pause in typing, a setting with its delay
Auto save on focus change saves a file as its editor loses the keys and when the terminal loses focus
Open Recent lists recently opened folders, then files, and opens the pick
The welcome page lists recent folders and files beside Start, and a click opens one

Run Task finds package.json, Cargo, Makefile, justfile, Go, pytest and tasks.json tasks, runs the pick in a pane tab named for it, and its compiler and test errors join Problems; Ctrl+Shift+B and Rerun Last Task
Errors from rustc and Cargo, tsc, ESLint, gcc and clang, Go and pytest are read into file, line and message
Settings' Keyboard section lists every command with its keys, searchable by name or keys; a click records new keys, saved in settings, with keys two commands share flagged

A file with merge conflicts shows each as a card, current green and incoming blue, its first line holding Compare, Both, Current and Incoming; Source Control lists the file under Merge Changes, offers Mark Resolved once no markers are left, and commits the merge
Next and Previous Conflict step through a file's conflicts, and Accept Current, Incoming or Both settle the one at the caret, from the palette
Source Control says when a merge, rebase, cherry-pick or revert is under way, and Abort abandons it after asking
Stash from Source Control's menu or the palette, with a message; stashes are listed under the changes, each showing what it holds and offering Apply, Pop and Drop
Dropping a stash, from its row or the palette's Drop Stash, asks first
Compare With compares the file in view, unsaved edits and all, with a branch, a recent commit or the clipboard in the diff view
Source Control ends with a graph of the repository's commits in lanes, merges as hollow dots; a commit opens to its files, each showing its diff against the commit before; Show Git History goes there
The Explorer's Timeline lists the commits that changed the file in view, each opening its diff there; Show File History lists them all

While Cellix is behind another window, an agent asking, a plan waiting, a finished turn, an answered comment or a failed test run becomes the terminal's own notification (OSC 777, 9 or 99, through tmux), one per event at most every 10 s, with a switch in Settings
The side pane's Inbox lists what waits in every workspace, newest first; a click goes to the workspace and opens it, the x lets it go, and empty it says what would fill it

"Needs you" means an agent asks something: Claude Code's idle reminder and sign-in notices don't count, a tool running clears an answered request, and an agent whose process has gone, or whose process started a new session, stops counting
An agent's transcript opens from its tab's right-click or the palette as a read-only page of its turns, prompts, replies and tool steps, with long output cut
Comment and Ask Agent on a transcript step tell the agent which turn and step it's about
A workspace's tile shows how full its fullest agent's context is, from the transcript's token counts

Agent Context in the sidebar: an agent's instructions in load order with imports, its skills, subagents, commands, hooks and MCP servers, what its last session read and how full its context got, and checks, each opening its file

Agents' hooks log each prompt with its session, agent, time and checkpoint, each plan version and answer, and each test run, and tasks are worked out from that log: a session split at a plan after an approved one
Show Agent Task: one page per task with its plan versions, turns, changes, tests and comments as a timeline
From the Task page a turn is reviewed on its own, read-only, and undone back to its checkpoint
A task can be split at a turn and renamed, and both are kept
The Task page links to the agent's transcript and shows how full its context grew over each turn, from the transcript
Every dialog and card button takes a click anywhere it's painted, edges included
Where the terminal reports cells, a dialog button is its row
A painted menu's items are clicked where their cells are
Every tooltip is one row, on a row of its own
Review letters its files as Source Control does, matches the sidebar's width, and ends each file with what's next
A comment kind with none is quiet and one with some is filled
The pane's tab is a chip inside its row
Code scrolls a row past its end, clear of the status bar
The light theme is Catppuccin Latte
A server refusing a background request (hints, folds, signatures) says nothing in the status bar
A page scrolled past its end keeps its scrollbar thumb inside its track, clear of a pane under the file
A paste the Windows console hands over in two reads stays one paste, so its last line break can't accept a suggestion
A narrow side pane's tabs stay clear of the icons at the top right; the one in front keeps its name and a chevron lists every tab
Section headings look one way in Source Control, the Timeline, Agent Context and the Task page: small quiet bold capitals, a chevron when they fold
Show Source, Compare, Clear Finished, Start an Agent and a language server's Install are quiet buttons, not bare words; Merging stands apart from its Abort button
Counts say "1 line", not "1 lines"; a commit, stash or comparison ends without asking for a commit
Source Control's commit box, its buttons and what's under way stay put while the lists under them scroll
A side pane standing under the file hides with the bottom-panel icon, its foot filled; beside the file, with the right-panel one
Your prompt on the Task page fills its box before it wraps, measured as the font draws it
Floating panels (palettes, signature help, suggestions) end on row lines and never cut through the text rows around them
An agent's context meter takes the window its Claude model has: a million for every current model, 200k only for Haiku 4.5 and older
Control characters in a file, an agent's output or a transcript show as their pictures and never reach the terminal
A fenced code block closes only on a fence of the same mark at least as long, so output holding ``` stays inside a transcript's block
Agent Context reads Codex's instructions as Codex does: the 32 KiB cut lands between characters, and an empty AGENTS.override.md is passed over
Neither Cellix nor an agent's hooks use a sockets folder someone else owns or can enter, so another user can't answer an agent as the reviewer
An agent can't reply to a comment as the reviewer, and a backslash in its reply arrives as it wrote it
What Cellix pastes into an agent can't end the paste early or send keys: control characters are dropped, and line breaks are line breaks
An agent stopped by an API error or an interrupt isn't left working, and an answered question isn't counted as needing you
File text and output in what an agent is told sit in quotes they can't close, so a line of code can't pass as the reviewer's words
A failed test run in Codex or Gemini CLI shows as failed: the exit code is read from JSON in a string or from the result's words, and with none the output decides
On the Task page, a prompt said again, as "continue", shows its own turn's context, not the first one's
A compacted Claude Code session gets no turn for its summary, and its meter stops showing the context from before the compaction
A tasks log line cut inside a character costs only that line, not the whole log
